analysis: What changed vs the 7 AM brief: futures firmed a touch — Dow +0.6% and S&P +0.75% per IBD's latest read vs +0.5%/+0.7% at 7 AM — while the Nasdaq held +0.7%. The genuinely new items since 7 AM are (1) the data-center financing freeze is now Bloomberg-confirmed, not just reported: a $6.6B Bridge Data Centres loan delayed, multiple banks reviewing or exiting loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, which hardens the export-control story from rumor into a credit event; (2) HP's +11.5% Wednesday surge on a tariff-refund-aided beat and dividend raise — a defensive, value-name rally inside a tech rout; (3) credit-market stress widening beyond equities, with CoreWeave's 5Y CDS spiking and record CDS prints for Nvidia, Oracle, Alphabet and SpaceX (single-source, PANews); (4) Meta's +3.4% Wednesday outperformance on the Muse/Amazon talks. Signal vs noise: the Bloomberg-confirmed loan freeze plus the FT-reported Nvidia shipment halt are signal — the Nov 19 BIS rule is now visibly choking the Southeast Asia compute-financing channel, which is exactly the demand Nvidia's bull case depends on; the CDS widening is corroborating signal from credit, not just equity noise. HP's jump is mostly relief in a heavily doubted name (tariff refunds supplied much of the beat), not a sector turn. Wednesday's Nasdaq 100 bear-market touch and reversal remains the context for Friday: the bounce is real but happened on turnover ~5% below the 20-day average, and Goldman's desk called it an abatement of supply rather than a wave of buying. No qualifying Hacker News or Reddit threads added signal beyond the headlines, so community_signals is empty. Cash markets closed today for Thanksgiving; everything hinges on Friday's thin half session.
disclaimer: Not financial advice — for informational purposes only.

headlines.headline: US index futures firmed slightly on Thanksgiving morning: Dow +0.6%, S&P 500 +0.75%, Nasdaq-100 +0.7% (IBD, latest read), vs +0.5%/+0.7%/+0.7% at 7 AM PT; cash markets closed for Thanksgiving, futures trade until 1 PM ET.
headlines.why_it_matters: The rebound is holding and inching higher into the holiday pause — but overnight futures on a closed market do not guarantee Friday's open, and Friday is a thin half session.

headlines.headline: Bloomberg confirms lenders have frozen billions in Asian data-center loans after the US chip curbs: the upsized $6.6B Bridge Data Centres loan (ByteDance customer) is delayed by extra due diligence, banks including Citi, Standard Chartered, DBS, OCBC and UOB are reviewing loans tied to ByteDance, Alibaba and Tencent, and at least one bank passed on a $372M Digital Halo loan; the FT-reported Nvidia server-shipment halt to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia stands.
headlines.why_it_matters: The export-control story graduated from headline risk to a credit event — the Nov 19 BIS rule is now visibly choking the Southeast Asia financing channel that feeds Nvidia-adjacent demand.

headlines.headline: HP (HPQ) was Wednesday's standout, jumping 11.49% to $31.15 after fiscal Q4 revenue rose 9.3% to $16.0B and non-GAAP EPS of $0.83 beat the $0.75 estimate; HP raised its quarterly dividend to $0.31 and Emma Walmsley takes over as CEO Jan 4, 2027. Tariff refunds added $0.15/share to the beat.
headlines.why_it_matters: A value/dividend name rallied hard while growth sold off — rotation into safety, though the beat was flattered by tariff refunds, so the move reads more as relief in a doubted stock than a sector turn.

headlines.headline: Wednesday's megacap closes: Apple $355.58 (+0.43%) the only Mag7 gainer besides Meta $609.89 (+3.40%); Nvidia $149.30 (-3.91%), Amazon $244.43 (-3.12%), Alphabet $273.10 (-2.13%), Microsoft $489.93 (-1.25%), Tesla $380.14 (-1.18%). Apple is November's Mag7 winner (+3.3% for the month, fifth straight monthly gain); Nvidia the month's worst.
headlines.why_it_matters: The AI trade is splitting — Apple's steadiness vs Nvidia's governance-driven slide — rather than moving as one block, and defensive inflows are favoring names with less AI-capex exposure.

headlines.headline: Meta rose 3.40% Wednesday, the best Mag7 print, with Third Point listing it as a top position and reports of talks to integrate Meta's Muse AI agent into Amazon's marketplace.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source on the Muse/Amazon talks — treat as fragile. If real, it would give Meta's agent a commercial distribution channel beyond its own apps.

headlines.headline: Credit markets showed more stress than equities Wednesday: CoreWeave's five-year CDS spiked to 15.34 points (over 70% implied default probability), and CDS for Nvidia, Oracle, Alphabet and SpaceX all hit record highs, with Goldman's data-center CDS basket also at a record.
headlines.why_it_matters: Single-source (PANews) — treat as fragile. If accurate, credit is pricing AI-infrastructure risk more severely than equity, a corroborating warning for the debt-funded buildout.

headlines.headline: Oil higher again after Houthi strikes on Saudi Red Sea ports: WTI futures $84.27 (+0.7%) after closing Wednesday at $83.68 (+2%), Brent near $95; copper jumped more than 3% off an 11-month low; silver topped $41 while gold slipped.
headlines.why_it_matters: A supply-threat premium is building in energy and metals alongside the equity rebound — a second front to watch into the OPEC+ meeting this weekend.

market_snapshot.breadth_notes: Prior session (Wed Nov 25): S&P 500 -0.25% to 7,182.78 after falling as much as 3.2% intraday; Nasdaq -0.62% to 23,585.80 after -4.6% intraday; Dow +0.33% to 50,182.95 after falling more than 1,100 points intraday; Russell 2000 +0.71%. Breadth was positive: ~372 advancers vs ~128 decliners, 8 of 11 sectors higher; equal-weight S&P +0.8%. Nasdaq 100's -4.7%-to--0.6% intraday reversal has been seen only 16 times since 1988; it briefly touched bear-market territory (-20% from its Oct 6 record). Turnover in S&P stocks was about 5% below the 20-day average (ZeroHedge). No cash session today — Thanksgiving.

WTI $84.27 is Thursday futures (+0.7%); gold $3,601.30 spot and Bitcoin ~$60,821 per FXStreet cross-asset snapshot.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC company news overnight. Carry-forward: a Nov 24 Zacks piece frames the growth case — $500M order book through 2029, >60% of 2027 new horsepower contracted, record $23.14/month revenue per horsepower (+8% y/y), with LNG exports and power demand seen needing 10M+ additional compression horsepower; a Nov 26 Seeking Alpha note rates USAC a Hold — 8.88% yield covered, but limited upside at 8.29x forward EV/EBITDA amid substantial debt — countering the Nov 25 buy-rated piece at $23.63 citing the 8.9% yield, 1.67x distribution coverage and record pricing. Q3 2026 (Nov 3): revenue $357.2M (+43% y/y, above ~$348.3M consensus), EPS $0.33/unit in line, adjusted EBITDA $197.3M, DCF $127.1M, coverage 1.67x; FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance narrowed to $770-780M; $0.525/unit quarterly distribution (annualized $2.10) paid Nov 6; Zacks raised FY2026 EPS estimate to $1.16 from $1.04 (Nov 24), FY2027 at $1.31. Next earnings Feb 16, 2027.
